summary: On Balance Volume: a running total that adds volume on up closes and subtracts it on down closes.
overview: On Balance Volume (OBV), by Joe Granville, is a running volume line in its own pane. It rises when volume comes on up closes and falls when it comes on down closes.
An optional moving average can be added as a smoothing or signal line.
how: If close is above the previous close, add the bar's volume. If below, subtract it. If equal, OBV stays the same.
The smoothing line can be SMA or another type, 20 bars by default. The level of OBV has no meaning by itself; the slope does.
use: Some traders watch OBV breaking out before price does.
Look for divergence between OBV and price.
Use the smoothing line to see when OBV turns.
Use it to check whether a breakout comes with rising volume.
alerts: Alerts: you can alert on its line crossing a value or the candle close (from the chart's + menu); checked while ZoroCharts is open.
notes: It needs volume data; on symbols without volume it shows nothing useful.
